input.title: judgment-eval cannot score a question-set version before it deploys
input.body:
judgment-eval runs a use case against whatever question-set version the server has deployed, and a dev server has no model key. A proposed version (vN+1) cannot be measured before it merges and deploys.

Measured on TKT-9601: a v2 set was gated, merged and deployed with its acceptance number recorded as n/a, because nothing could produce it earlier. The post-deploy eval then failed the bar set in advance, so the change had to be reverted in prod. A pre-merge measurement would have stopped it at the PR.

Every future "propose question-set vN+1" ticket hits the same gap.

Fix direction: let judgment-eval score a candidate set that is not the deployed one, scored without recording product calls. Regression test: an eval naming a non-deployed candidate scores against that version, and a version it cannot load is an error, not a silent fallback.

input.title: credo no_unscoped_log_emptiness cannot see a generic phrase bound to an attribute or variable
input.body:
The widened credo check from TKT-9602 flags a literal phrase refuted on a whole log capture in an async test module. It does not see a phrase that is first bound to a module attribute or variable and then refuted.

Measured by the TKT-9602 captain: one summaries test refutes an attribute holding a generic sentence unscoped, and a sibling test's body text differs from it by one capital letter. It is not a collision today, but it is one edit away from a cross-test false failure, and the check cannot flag it.

Fix direction: extend the check to resolve an attribute or local binding to its literal before judging, or scope those refutes so the class is closed for bound values too. Regression test: a bound generic phrase refuted on a whole capture in an async module is flagged; a scoped one is not.

input.title: check-forge-stub-guard cannot see stubs written through helper functions
input.body:
Impact: the stub guard flags a stub write only when the tool's name is written literally (or by a for-loop over names) as a redirection or copy target. A stub written through a helper function, such as a suite's stub_claude <path> or a cat >"$1/git" in a setup function, is invisible to it. TKT-9603 converted two such suites by hand, but a new suite of that shape passes the check unguarded and can reach the live tool.

Fix: model stub-writing helper functions: a function whose body writes "$N/<tool>" and each call of it whose argument is a directory later put on PATH counts as a stub write at the call's line. Regression test: a fixture suite with stub_git() { cat >"$1/git"; } and PATH="$d:$PATH" and no guard fails the check.

input.title: UniqueIndexAudit checks one direction: it never finds a unique index no changeset declares
input.body:
Found while TKT-9604. Impact now: the unique-index audit checks one direction only. It confirms that every declared unique constraint names a real index. It never finds a unique index that no changeset declares, which is the defect class of two earlier tickets (a duplicate insert raises a constraint error instead of returning a changeset error). Nothing is wrong today because of it; it is a check gap.

Measured on the test database: 20 tables have a unique index with no changeset declaration. Each is written today only through upserts, insert_all or update_all on non-key columns, so none is reachable now.

Fix: add the reverse direction: every non-pkey unique index maps to a declaration in its schema's changeset, or to an explicit upsert-only allowlist entry. Test the miss: a table with an undeclared unique index fails the audit.

input.title: Cron installers: worktree refusal is exit 3 in one installer, exit 4 in another
input.body:
Impact: the same refusal (an installer run from a linked worktree) is exit 3 in one cron installer script and exit 4 in a sibling. Both are documented, but a caller cannot branch on one code for one condition across the installers.

Fix: pick one exit code for the worktree refusal across the cron installers, update each --help and its tests. Found by the TKT-9605 captain.

input.title: IDLE_WORKFLOW_RE duplicated in two config classes
input.body:
Impact: the idle_workflow validation regex is copied byte for byte in two classes. A third reader was added to the first by TKT-9606. A later change to one copy leaves the other accepting or refusing different values, and nothing says so.

Fix: one home for the regex, and the second class references it. Grep every other idle_workflow validation in the same change. Regression test: a value refused by one is refused by the other.

input.title: shipwright self-test calls next_second before defining it
input.body:
Impact: the suite calls next_second near line 2000, before the function is defined near line 2100. Every run prints `next_second: command not found`, and that case never gets the one-second separation it meant to have, so it tests a different timing than it says. Pre-existing on main.

Fix: define next_second before its first use, and make an undefined helper fail the suite rather than print and continue. Regression test: the suite fails when a helper is called before its definition.

input.title: main red: check-pipefail-grep fails on 19 grep -q pipes in a self-test
input.body:
Impact: custom origin/main is RED at a recent commit. The post-landing gate fails 1 of 177 checks, check-pipefail-grep, on 19 `... | grep -q` pipes in a self-test that runs under `set -o pipefail`. Under pipefail, grep -q exiting early can SIGPIPE the writer and flip a passing assertion to a failure, so these are flaky assertions. While main is red, pushes to main are refused.

Fix: convert the 19 sites to here-strings, per the check's own Fix. Regression evidence: the check fails on the red commit and passes on the fix.

input.title: JudgmentFeedback.changeset/1 missing unique_constraint for (call_id, reporter)
input.body:
A class-wide audit of constraint declarations found a gap in the feedback changeset. The migration creates a unique index on (call_id, reporter), but the changeset declares no unique_constraint for that pair.

Not exercised today: the only writer always upserts with on_conflict and a conflict_target, which Postgres matches by column list, so the upsert works whether or not the changeset declares the constraint. But a future caller doing a bare insert on a duplicate pair would raise a constraint error instead of returning {:error, changeset}, because the changeset has nothing to catch it.

Fix: add the unique_constraint with the index's real name, with a regression test modeled on the earlier ticket's.

input.title: Weekly summary double counts a task after a retried delivery
input.body:
When the summary job is retried after a timeout, a task that was already counted in the first attempt is counted again, so the weekly total shows 14 tasks when the workspace has 12. The wrong number is sent to the owner every Monday that a retry happens.

Reproduced on TKT-9611 with a forced timeout on the first attempt. Fix: count by task id, not by delivery attempt. Regression test: a retried run reports the same total as an unretried one.

input.title: lead-time report crashes with nil error when the ledger has no rows
input.body:
Running the lead-time report in a repo with an empty ledger raises `undefined method 'sort_by' for nil` and exits 1 with a stack trace. The documented behaviour for an empty ledger is to print "no rows" and exit 0. Seen on TKT-9612 in a fresh checkout.

Fix: treat a missing rows list as empty. Regression test: an empty ledger prints "no rows" and exits 0.

input.title: check-pipefail-grep misses `| grep -qE` pipes, which its header says it flags
input.body:
The check's header says it flags every `| grep -q` style pipe in a script that runs under `set -o pipefail`, including the -E, -F and -i variants. It flags `| grep -q` but passes `| grep -qE 'x'` and `| grep -qi x`, so a script with those pipes goes green although the header promises a failure.

Found on TKT-9613: a suite with three `grep -qE` pipes passed the check. Fix: match grep with any combination of flags that includes q. Regression test: a fixture with `| grep -qE` fails the check.

input.title: A second webhook event with the same delivery id is dropped, not applied
input.body:
The webhook handler dedupes on the delivery id, but it records the id before it applies the event. When the apply step fails and the sender retries, the retry carries the same id, is treated as a duplicate and acknowledged, and the event is lost for good. Seen on TKT-9614: one status change never reached the tracker.

Fix: record the id in the same transaction as the apply. Regression test: a failed apply followed by a retry applies the event once.
